title: Many shall come from the east and west and sit down with Abraham — the centurion who heard, and the house gathered from every quarter (Isaiah 11; Psalm 107; Luke 13)
summary:
It ain't new. A centurion in Capernaum asks for a word and not a visit, and Yahusha (Jesus) marvels:

*When Yahusha (Jesus) heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 8:10)

Not in Yashar'el (Israel) means not in the house at home. Luke tells who this soldier was before he ever sent for him:

*For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.* (Luke 7:5)

A Roman officer who loved the nation and built its synagogue, who called himself unworthy of a visit and trusted the word alone. The sheep hear the voice because they are sheep:

*My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:* (John 10:27)

That is how the man reads: not a stranger whose faith shames the house, but one of the house found out among the nations, known by his hearing. And it is why the next words are about a gathering and not about a replacing:

*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11)

The prophets had already said who comes from the east and the west, and from where:

*And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* (Isaiah 11:12)

*And gathered them out of the lands, from the east, and from the west, from the north, and from the south.* (Psalm 107:3)

*Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim.* (Isaiah 49:12)

The ones gathered are the outcasts and the dispersed, the two houses brought back from every quarter. The table they sit at is the feast the prophet set on the mountain:

*And in this mountain shall Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined.* (Isaiah 25:6)

And the name made great in every place is the name carried by the scattered where they were driven:

*For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* (Malachi 1:11)

Then the hard word:

*But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 8:12)

This is not the house put away for the nations. It is the sifting of the house: the ones who had the kingdom in hand and would not do the Father's will, thrust out while the fathers and the gathered sit down. Luke keeps the same scene with the same two halves:

*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of Elohim (God), and you yourselves thrust out.* (Luke 13:28)

*And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Luke 13:29)

And Paul closes the door on the misreading:

*I say then, Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.* (Romans 11:1)

A centurion heard, and the house was not cast away. The feast fills with the scattered coming home from every direction, and empties of the ones at home who would not hear.

121850.prose: The many who sit down with Abraham sit down at this table. Isaiah set the feast on the mountain and spread it *unto all people*, and the ones Yahusha (Jesus) says will come to it come *from the east and west*, the directions the prophets give for the scattered coming home. The feast is the gathering's table, laid before the gathering began.
121850.phrase: make unto all people a feast of fat things
121850.sentence: The mountain feast of fat things is the table the many from east and west sit down to with the fathers.

2547.prose: Isaiah's *these shall come from far* is said of the people Yahuah (the LORD) is bringing back, named by the quarters they come from: the north, the west, the land of Sinim. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same directions for the many who will sit with Abraham. The compass points are not a figure for the nations; they are where the house was scattered to.
2547.sentence: These from far, from the north and the west and the land of Sinim: the scattered named by the quarters they return from.

121852.prose: The psalm says who is gathered *from the east, and from the west*, and from the north and the south too: the redeemed of Yahuah (the LORD), *whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy* (Psalm 107:2). The many who come from east and west to sit with the fathers are those redeemed, gathered out of the lands they were driven into. Not strangers added to the house; the house brought home.
121852.sentence: The redeemed gathered out of the lands from all four quarters: the many from east and west are the house coming home.

121853.prose: Malachi hears that the name will be great *among the Gentiles* from the sun's rising to its going down, with a pure offering in every place. The centurion is a man in whom that was already so, a Roman who loved the nation and built its synagogue, and who trusted the word. Where the scattered went, the name went with them, and the many from east and west come back from those same places.
121853.phrase: my name shall be great among the Gentiles
121853.sentence: The name great among the Gentiles from sunrise to sunset: the name carried by the scattered where they were driven, and a centurion who had it.

121854.prose: *The children of the kingdom shall be cast out* has been read as the house of Yashar'el (Israel) put away for the nations. Paul answers that reading before it starts: *Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid*, and offers himself, of the seed of Abraham, as the proof. The casting out here is the sifting of the house, the unhearing thrust out while the gathered sit down; the house itself is not cast away.
121854.phrase: Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid.
121854.sentence: Has Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid: the guard on the children of the kingdom cast out.

121855.prose: The ones cast out into outer darkness are children of the kingdom who would not hear, not the people Elohim (God) foreknew. Paul says it in one line: he *hath not cast away his people which he foreknew*. The weeping at the door is the sifting of the house, some thrust out while the fathers and the gathered sit down, and the people as a people stand where they stood.
121855.phrase: Elohim (God) hath not cast away his people which he foreknew
121855.sentence: Not cast away, the people he foreknew: the casting out at the feast is of the unhearing, not of the house.

5513.prose: Luke sets the same gathering after the question whether few are saved, and adds the two quarters Matthew leaves out, the north and the south: all four directions to the one table, the kingdom of Elohim (God). Beside it Luke keeps the other half of Matthew's saying too, the ones at home who see the fathers seated *and you yourselves thrust out* (Luke 13:28). The gathering and the sifting stand together in both gospels.
5513.sentence: From all four quarters to the kingdom of Elohim (God): Luke's telling of the same gathering, with the sifting beside it.
